verses.text: Asa's son Jehoshaphat became king after him. He made his kingdom strong against Israel.
He put soldiers in all the walled towns of Judah. He also put army camps in the land of Judah and in the towns of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
The LORD was with Jehoshaphat, because he lived the way his ancestor David had lived in his early years. He did not worship the Baal gods.
Instead he looked to the God of his father and obeyed his commands. He did not act like the people of Israel.
So the LORD made the kingdom strong under his control. All the people of Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, and he had great wealth and honor.
His heart was proud to follow the LORD's ways. He also removed the hilltop shrines and the Asherah poles from Judah.
In the third year of his rule, he sent his officials Ben Hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah to teach in the towns of Judah.
With them he sent some Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tobadonijah. He also sent the priests Elishama and Jehoram with them.
They taught the people in Judah, and they had the book of the LORD's law with them. They went around to all the towns of Judah and taught the people.
The fear of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms around Judah, so they did not go to war against Jehoshaphat.
Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as payment. The Arabs also brought him flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
Jehoshaphat became more and more powerful. He built forts and storage towns in Judah.
He had a lot of supplies in the towns of Judah, and he kept brave, experienced soldiers in Jerusalem.
Here is the list of them by their families. From Judah, the commanders of thousands were: Adnah the commander, with three hundred thousand brave soldiers;
next, Jehohanan the commander, with two hundred eighty thousand;
next, Amasiah son of Zichri, who gladly offered himself to serve the LORD, with two hundred thousand brave soldiers.
From Benjamin: Eliada, a brave soldier, with two hundred thousand men armed with bows and shields;
next, Jehozabad, with one hundred eighty thousand men ready for war.
These were the men who served the king, besides the soldiers he put in the walled towns all over Judah.
